newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Explorers Index slumps on RBA gold sale.
newsitem.headline: Australian Explorers Index slumps on RBA gold sale.

text.p: Perth stockbroker Eyres Reed Ltd said its Australian Explorers Index fell 258.2 points or 8.66 percent last week. The All Ordinaries Index fell 1.25 percent.
July 11 July 4 pct 1 Month pct 1 Year pct
NOTE: The explorers index (base 500, March 1992) tracks the performance of 88 small capitalisation exploration companies.

Eyres Reed analyst Glen Colgan said in a commentary that the index suffered heavily last week from the confidence-undermining admission by the Reserve Bank of Australia that it had sold two-thirds of the country's gold reserves.

The Index was over 500 points lower on Tuesday before closing the week 258.2 points down. An absence of buyers and desperate sellers resulted in falls outnumbering gains by six to one in relatively thin trade.

Best performers included Wells Gold, up three cents to 12 cents, recently-reconstructed Aquarius up 17 cents to 72 cents, Denehurst up 0.8 cents to 7.5 cents, Haoma three cents higher at 31 cents and Gindalbie up two cents to 22 cents.

Falls were dominated by gold hopefuls, including Merritt Mining NL down 3.5 cents to nine cents, Marymia Exploraiton NL off six cents to 17 cents, Nugold Hill Mines NL down three cents to 8.5 cents, Troy Resources NL dropped 37 cents to 90 cents and Border Gold Ltd 6.5 cents lower at 13 cents.

The week's worst performer was Sipa Resources, who announced that metallurgical test work had left grave doubts about the economic viability of the Mt Olympus prospect in Western Australia. A bad week for bad news, the share price fell 25.5 cents to 18 cents.
